purpose: North-star composition for the redesigned homepage
prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: revised high-fidelity desktop homepage approval comp
Input image: the referenced project-only Systems Atlas homepage is the edit target.
Primary request: Keep the exact contemporary Systems Atlas visual identity, central ANSON LIN interchange, enamel off-white map ground, cobalt/green/international-orange route grammar, carbon-black wayfinding typography, spatial hierarchy, and production craft. Redesign the homepage information architecture so the map is about Anson's profile, not projects.
Replace the three project stations and all project titles with exactly four profile stations: Skills, Background, Learnings, and Target. Use four disciplined routes: cobalt, green, international orange, and carbon black. The first viewport contains only the central Anson identity card and those four profile stations. No project names, screenshots, cards, technologies, project metrics, or project showcase appear anywhere in the homepage body.
Top navigation exact items: HOME, SKILLS, BACKGROUND, LEARNINGS, CASE STUDIES, CONTACT. CASE STUDIES is only a compact navigation destination for separate project pages, not a homepage section.
Central card exact text: ANSON LIN, Graduate Software Engineer, Auckland, New Zealand, I build dependable full-stack products and tested systems. Change primary action to exact text Explore my profile. Keep Download resume.
Below the map, flow directly into the visible beginning of the Skills section. Show a calm, route-led skills layout with headings only such as Backend, Frontend, Testing, and Tools; do not show project cards, screenshots, fake interfaces, or project names. The Skills section should visibly continue the same transit geometry at a quieter reading scale.
Motion implied: the four profile routes draw once from the central interchange; selecting a station scrolls to its corresponding homepage section. The Case Studies navigation opens a compact list of the separate case-study routes.
Invariants: preserve the reference image's color, type character, station shapes, map texture, exact spacing discipline, clear actions, and 1440x1000 landscape website framing.
Constraints: no portrait or invented likeness; no project showcase on the homepage; no Engineering Proof section or proof labels; no invented employers, clients, metrics, testimonials, skills, or claims; no pixel art, dark mode, glassmorphism, gradients, bento cards, serif editorial style, code-editor screenshot, lorem ipsum, or watermark.
nonliteral: The generated Target station label is malformed; production copy must read Target.
All interface text and route geometry must be semantic HTML, CSS, and SVG rather than rasterized UI.
The comp establishes desktop composition; mobile uses a vertical route with the same reading order.
